artists.biography:
The group was formed by guitarist, singer and chief songwriter Bill Fisher and keyboardist Michael Wetherburn over a mutual love of musical theatre and Queen. The group members had previously played in various bands in and around Nottingham, and a number of early songs by the group had been written years before while in other bands. Fisher was more interested in progressive pop rather than progressive rock, and wanted the band to be primarily about good songwriting over pointless technical ability. His influences include The Beatles, Kate Bush, David Bowie and Peter Gabriel, The instrumentation makes prominent use of the Hammond organ.

The band is signed to Bilocation Records. They have also covered Pink Floyd's "The Trial" on Magnetic Eye Records' tribute album The Wall Redux. Fisher has described the group as a "twofold entity: a new religious movement…and a 7-piece supergroup".

In 2017, the group released "Evil in your Eye" from their first album Is Satan Real? on 21 August to coincide with the solar eclipse on the same day.
Bill Fisher - guitar, vocals
Joanne Joyce - vocals
Caroline Cawley - vocals
Michael Wetherburn - keyboards, vocals
Amy Nicholson - cello, vocals
Sam Lloyd - bass
Loz Stone - drums

perplexity.description:
Church of the Cosmic Skull's second studio album Science Fiction was released in May 2018 on Kozmik Artifactz as a limited edition heavyweight vinyl and CD. The seven-piece Nottingham ensemble continued their exploration of progressive rock with ambitious arrangements that drew comparisons to classic acts like Queen and Queens of the Stone Age. The album marked the band's second release after their 2016 debut Is Satan Real?, establishing their signature sound of layered vocals, expansive instrumentation, and conceptual depth.

Science Fiction represented a continuation of the band's artistic vision while refining their approach to progressive rock composition. The album featured the band's characteristic multi-vocal arrangements and complex instrumental interplay, with contributions from guitarists Bill Fisher and Martyn Fisher, keyboardist Michael Wetherburn, and a full ensemble of supporting musicians. The release demonstrated the group's commitment to independent operations, as they maintained creative control through their choice of label and production approach rather than pursuing major label interest.

The album received positive critical reception within progressive rock circles, building on the momentum established by their debut. Science Fiction solidified Church of the Cosmic Skull's reputation as a distinctive voice in contemporary prog rock, setting the stage for their subsequent releases including Everybody's Going To Die in 2019, which would garner further acclaim from publications like Mojo and recognition from media figures like Jonathan Ross.
